● Industry news · 3 min read

⚡ Does a project-specific liability policy cover work after the job is built?

A liability insurer doesn't have to defend the builders of a Texas toll road in lawsuits over a 130-car pileup, because the suits were about running the road, not building it.

✅ Not always. A policy written for one project's construction work may not cover claims about what happens after the project is done, such as operating or maintaining it.

✅ In a ruling reported Oct 29, 2026, Liberty Mutual was found to have no duty to defend the builders of a Fort Worth toll road in lawsuits over a 2021 pileup that killed six people.

● Market outlook · 2 min read

☂️ Is U.S. construction spending down? What the September 2026 numbers show

Total spending fell in September and is down for the year. The drop is almost all residential. Nonresidential work, where most commercial contractors live, is still growing.

✅ Yes. U.S. construction spending ran at a seasonally adjusted annual rate of $2,186.1 billion in September 2026, down 1.9% from August and 2.7% from a year earlier, the Census Bureau reported Nov 2.

✅ Spending for the first nine months of 2026 was $1,649.6 billion, 2.9% below the same period in 2025.

● COI basics · 5 min read

✅ What does waiver of subrogation mean on a contractor COI?

It's the insurer's promise not to come after you once it pays a claim. A waiver of subrogation comes from an endorsement such as WC 00 03 13, not from the SUBR WVD box on the certificate, and it has to match a contract the contractor signed before the loss.

✅ A waiver of subrogation is the insurer's acknowledgment that it has no right to recover what it paid from a liable third party, such as the owner or GC.

✅ Insurers agree to it because their insured already gave up its own right of recovery in a contract. Policies generally allow that before a loss, not after.

● COI basics · 5 min read

✅ Will a COI give you notice of cancellation if a contractor's policy lapses mid-project?

Usually not. Since 2009, the notice of cancellation box on the ACORD 25 only points back to the policy, and the policy usually sends notice to the contractor, not you. If coverage lapses mid-project, you may find out after a claim, and in some states the GC pays the injured worker's benefits.

✅ Usually not. Since the 2009/09 edition, the ACORD 25 cancellation box says only that notice "will be delivered in accordance with the policy provisions."

✅ Standard policy provisions send cancellation notice to the named insured, the contractor, not to the certificate holder.

● COI basics · 5 min read

✅ Does additional insured status cover you after the job is done? Completed operations, CG 20 10 and CG 20 37

Not with CG 20 10 alone. Since 1993, the standard additional insured endorsement covers only the contractor's ongoing operations. For claims about finished work, you need completed operations coverage from a second endorsement, usually CG 20 37, and it's the form most often missing from a contractor COI.

✅ CG 20 10 covered finished work until its 1993 edition. Every edition since covers only ongoing operations.

✅ CG 20 37 exists only to add additional insured status for completed operations. It doesn't cover the work in progress.
